subject.who: A gentleman, a soldier (his name is withheld by Lilly)
subject.background: He propounded six demands at once.
subject.question: (1) If he were like to live long, yea or no? (2) To what part of the world he were best to direct his course of life? (3) What part of his life was in probability like to be most fortunate? (4) What general accidents had happened unto him already? (5) What accidents in future he might expect, good or ill? (6) The time when?
subject.moment: Not stated in the chapter (no dated figure heading is given in the text).

chart_data.ascendant: Leo (sign ascending; a fixed star of the first magnitude, Cor Leonis/Regulus, in 24°34′ of Leo neer the cusp of the first house)
chart_data.key_positions: The Sun, lord of the Ascendant, in Aries 4°18′ in the ninth house, in his exaltation, two degrees ten minutes distant from the cusp of the ninth; the Moon in Virgo in the second house applying to a trine of Jupiter; Jupiter and Venus in Taurus in the tenth house; Mars in the eighth house; the Moon wanting 7°22′ of the opposition of Mars
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the OCR glyphs for the signs are corrupt and degrees are recorded only where the prose prints them numerically.

subject.who: A citizen of London (the querent), asking concerning his absent brother
subject.background: In November 1645 the brother was gone into the west of England, and no news had been heard of him for many weeks, the kingdom at that time being full of soldiers.
subject.question: (1) If living or dead; if dead, whether killed by soldiers? (2) When should he hear of him, and where was he? (3) When would he come home?
subject.moment: November 1645, about 4 p.m. London time: the question was asked the same day the trine of Venus and Saturn perfected — Lilly finds in the ephemeris the true time of the aspect at five of the clock that afternoon, 'but with reduction to our London Meridian little after four'.

chart_data.key_positions: Venus, lady of the third house (significatrix of the absent brother), in no manner of way afflicted either by Mercury, lord of the eighth in the figure, or by Mars; Venus applying to a trine of Saturn, lord of the Ascendant; Venus leaving a northern sign and entering into a south sign, wanting one degree of leaving the sign
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; one scheme serves the three queries (printed as Figs. 7–8 in the 1852 edition).

subject.background: She desired resolution whether the child she went with was a boy or a girl, and how long it would be before her delivery.
subject.question: (1) Is the child a boy or a girl? (2) How long ere she should be delivered?

chart_data.key_positions: Eight testimonies of a male child against four of a female among the proper significators (1647 count); Saturn, lord of the fifth, in Aries 24°37′; the Moon in Capricorn 9°50′, her distance from the opposition of Saturn being 14°47′; Mercury, lord of the Ascendant, in Aries 11°00′, his distance from the body of Saturn 13°37′; the two distances differing by only one degree ten minutes, and a degree allowed for a week
chart_data.note: Positions and testimony counts as printed in the 1647 text; see the ocr_note for the differing count in the 1852 edition.

subject.who: A sick doctor (the patient; the question asked concerning him)
subject.background: A decumbiture-type sickness question: the doctor was ill, and Lilly, having little judgment in physic himself, judged from the figure and afterwards spoke with the patient.
subject.question: What was his disease? If curable? What part of the body was afflicted?

chart_data.key_positions: The sixth house afflicted by a planet in his fall placed therein; the lord of the Ascendant lately separated from a dexter square of Saturn, Saturn at that time in Cancer (signifying the breast and stomach); the Moon in the fourth house with Saturn; all the angles fixed
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

subject.background: A sickness question on the figure of 16 July 1645; Lilly judged both the disease and the event, and persuaded the man to settle his affairs.
subject.question: Whether the sick would live or die, and what his disease was?
subject.moment: 16 July 1645 (figure heading; see the ocr_note on the year).

chart_data.key_positions: The Ascendant most afflicted by the corporal presence of a planet who is partly lord of the eighth house; the sign of the sixth fixed and afflicted, and the lord of the sixth in a fixed, earthly, melancholy sign; the Sun, the temporal light, in perfect opposition of Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs; the Moon neer the Dragon's Tail (Cauda Leonis in the OCR) and afflicted in the Ascendant
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the ascending sign's glyph is corrupt in the OCR and is not asserted here.

subject.who: A woman (the querent), of tall stature, ruddy complexioned, sober, discreet and well spoken
subject.background: She desired to marry a particular man, who was very tall, slender and lean, of black hair, stood upon high terms, and had been tampering with another.
subject.question: If she should marry the man desired?
subject.moment: Anno 1646 (figure heading fragment); the day is not legible in the OCR.

chart_data.key_positions: Mercury, significatrix of the querent, retrograde and under the Sun-beams; the quesited's significator in his exaltation, neer the sextile of Venus; both significators in a semi-sextile and in good houses; the Moon separating from a square of Jupiter and carrying his light by a trine to Mercury, lord of the Ascendant
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

subject.who: William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury (the quesited), then a prisoner
subject.background: The Archbishop was imprisoned and his fate in question during the Civil War; Lilly professes he honoured the man and never had speech or acquaintance with him.
subject.question: What manner of death should Canterbury die?

chart_data.key_positions: The cusp of the ninth house taken for his Ascendant (he being a man of the Church); Saturn, lord of that sign, in his fall, a long time retrograde, and posited in the twelfth of the figure; the Moon separating from Saturn and applying to the Sun neer the cusp of the eighth house; the Sun in a fiery sign applying to an opposition of Mars, the dispositor of the aged Bishop; Mars in an airy and humane sign; the Moon wanting seven degrees of the body of Mars
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the ascending degree is not given in the prose and is not asserted here.

subject.who: Prince Rupert (the quesited); the querent a very great well-willer to the Parliament
subject.background: Asked in time of war, about a month after the fight at Edgehill (23 October 1642), in which Essex had the better and kept the ground.
subject.question: If Prince Rupert should get honour by our wars, or worst the Earl of Essex? What should become of him?
subject.moment: Not stated in the chapter; internal evidence (Edgehill fight 'above a moneth before') places it about November–December 1642.

chart_data.key_positions: Rupert, as a noble person of eminency, signified by the tenth house and its lord, the Sun, peregrine and in his detriment in a fixed sign; Essex signified by Venus, lady of the opposite house, in reception with Saturn, she disposing of Rupert's significator; the Moon casting her sinister aspect to the cusp of the tenth; Venus also casting a dexter aspect to the cusp of the tenth
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

subject.who: King Charles I and Queen Henrietta Maria (the quesiteds); the querent unnamed
subject.background: One figure answering two war questions: whether the King would procure Irish forces against the Parliament, and whether the Queen, then in the North with an army, would advance, prosper, and meet the King.
subject.question: (1) If his Majesty should procure forces out of Ireland to harm the Parliament? (2) If the Queen, then in the North, would advance with her army, prosper, and when his Majesty should meet her?
subject.moment: Not stated in the chapter; the figure precedes the crossing of 11 April 1643 referred to in the judgment.

chart_data.key_positions: His Majesty signified by the Moon in Cancer in the tenth house, in her own house, increasing in light, and void of all infelicity except slowness in motion; the Sun, lord of the eleventh (the house signifying assistance or aid), posited in the seventh in his exaltation, applying to the cusp of the eleventh but wanting six degrees of being partill, and in direct opposition to the Ascendant (the Parliament); the Queen's significatrix Saturn, lord of the fourth (being the seventh from the tenth), removing out of one sign into another and going into Aries, his fall; the Moon wanting three or four degrees of the trine of Saturn
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

source.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II

subject.who: A gentleman (the querent) seeking an office or place of preferment
subject.background: The figure was erected at the same time, within four or five minutes, as the preceding figure (the King's Irish forces and the Queen's advance). He employed as his friend a solar man.
subject.question: If he should obtain the office or place he looked after (if attain the preferment desired)?
subject.moment: The same time, within four or five minutes, as the preceding figure; no separate date is stated.

chart_data.key_positions: The Ascendant and Venus for the querent; the tenth house for the office or place of preferment; the Moon placed in the tenth, applying to a trine of Saturn, who hath exaltation in the Ascendant, receives Venus and is received of her again; Saturn also lord of the fourth; the Sun in the seventh house in opposition to the Ascendant and with the Dragon's Tail, he being lord of the eleventh (the pretended friend); the Moon separating from a square of Mercury
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

subject.who: A sick person (the patient), asked about by others
subject.background: The physicians had prescribed much physic and it wrought no effect, but the patient was worse and worse, which gave those that asked some reason to suspect witchcraft.

subject.background: Her husband was imprisoned (in a garrison, in time of war); she asked when he should be delivered, and was told she need make no friends for his delivery.

subject.who: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, Lord General of the Parliament's army
subject.background: An event figure (not a posed question): the scheme of the time of the Earl's last setting forth into the West in 1644, judged by Lilly for posterity.
subject.question: Event figure: what success, honour and issue should the Earl have from this his last expedition into the West?
subject.moment: The time of his Excellency the Earl of Essex his last setting forth into the West, 1644 (event moment; the day is not stated in the text).

chart_data.key_positions: Saturn, Venus and Mercury having dignities in the Ascendant; the Moon separating from a trine of Saturn and applying to a square of Mars, lord of his (the Earl's) second and ninth houses (substance, assistants, friends, journeys); the Dragon's Tail in the Ascendant; Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, peregrine and in his fall in the second; the Moon in her detriment; the Part of Fortune disposed by Mercury, lord of the seventh, a significator of his enemies
chart_data.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.
